input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: No express liquidated damages clause exists, but Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights," which functions as a Customer-payable liquidated amount: we would owe the full committed spend for Services never taken, including after termination, and it conflicts with our termination rights in Sections 9.3, 9.4, and 27.3. Our preferred position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, so we deleted the take-or-pay penalty and limited payment to Services actually ordered and received; the fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

proposal.summary: Remove take-or-pay penalty; Customer pays only for Services ordered and received, with no liquidated damages or early-termination fee
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the take-or-pay commitment that would require us to pay for Services we do not take or that we terminate, because our position is that no liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum termination fees are payable by Customer. If a volume commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount, preserving our termination rights in Sections 9.3, 9.4, and 27.3.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer's purchase commitments, if any, are those stated in the applicable Order Form. Customer pays only for Services actually ordered and received and owes no take-or-pay amount, minimum fee, liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination charge, and this Section does not limit Customer's reduction or termination rights under this Agreement.
